best_parts: nodes start..asm: a five-rung ladder (stem, outflow, flow direction, cause and effect, fifth, assemble). Every idea is committed to before it is told, and the assemble probe re-tests TR1, TR14 and TR3 in a new form.
nodes s3_t2 and s3_t1: wrong-model feedback runs tempting reason, refutation, 'which follows from the pressure load?' nudge, plus a sure_note. This is the E3 repair done well.
nodes d3 and d4 (with d2): the deeper branch drills TR17 (arch share and the incidence pairing from K80, a verified claim). The other variants barely touch incidence.
flaws: node start: the trap options (infundibular stenosis, RVH) are weak against a learner who simply knows ASD is not in the four. Neither is an option a tired student would be drawn to. The same holds for pent_t3b (a second VSD loses to PDA) and d1_t2 (Turner loses to Down).
No fast lane and no different second explanation. Every miss gets the same 'Try again' loop, and recovery is never re-tested after the probe's own retry (the re-test comes only at asm).
R7: no clinical vignette anywhere in the core path. It is all abstract anatomy stems.

best_parts: nodes q1, q2, q3 option wording: each option states a reason (for example 'pumps against the outflow obstruction, at systemic pressure' versus 'thick RV muscle is a primary malformation'). A pick therefore says which causal model the learner holds, which is good for diagnosticity.
node q4: echo-report vignette for the accompanying ASD, with the 'secondary yet still the fourth component' trap on the thick RV wall.
node wrap: a one-line chain recap marked as a device.
flaws: node intro: tells all four components before any probe. This breaks ask-before-tell, and q2's stem also gives away the answer (it states 'infundibular, also called sub-pulmonary' before asking).

Wrong answers on q1 to q7 go to 'Next', not a retry. The learner never re-commits on the missed idea, so the miss is not repaired. Later probes (q6, q7) partly re-test it, but the same-probe retry is gone.
node d1: the stem names 6% and 15% as the wrong figures, so the key (20-25%) is found by elimination. The deeper branch has no incidence probe (K80).

gates: G1: node m1_t1 says 'the pentalogy name uses [ASD]' but cites only K13. That fact belongs to K5, which K13 does not say.
best_parts: node m1: the 'classmate's belief' frame makes each option a named wrong model, and the sure_note on the traps teaches both the PYQ key and the source (K77).
node recap and the m1..m5 order: a compact chain with one belief per probe.
node d1_t: refutes by saying where the confusable figures belong (22q11.2 share), and cites K79.
flaws: node m1_t1: the option 'keep ASD as the fourth component; PDA is the extra' is oddly worded, and its feedback adds a pentalogy fact without K5.
nodes m2 and m4: m4 has only two options and no hint, so it is a 50% guess. m2 has no hint option. The deeper branch has no incidence probe (K80).
node d1: the stem hands over the wrong figures (6% and 15%), so the key is findable by elimination.

merge_ideas: Take a's ladder (start, s1, s2, s3, pent, asm) as the spine. Swap in b's reason-bearing option wording at s3 and asm, so each choice names a causal model. Replace the weak start-probe distractors with c's classmate-belief framing, which makes a stronger opener.
Add b's echo-report vignette (q4) as a clinical re-test between pent and asm, to fix a's R7.
Keep a's deeper branch (d1..d4, including the K80 incidence pairing) and take c's d1_t trick of locating a confusable figure where it belongs.
Add a fast lane: if start is answered correctly and confidently, skip to pent. This needs the s1..s3 chain to stay guaranteed on the fall-through path, so the O2 objective is still covered.
